account: It is day 0, just after ten, and I have reached the plaza for my scheduled market walk. So far I have no concrete evidence of unusual activity. My suspicion that something is happening without me remains only a feeling. The secretary said there was no correspondence or unusual news. There was a brief misunderstanding about the appointment book after I returned it, but I saw the secretary retrieve it; that seems ordinary rather than suspicious. The builder came to the office carrying a lantern to discuss this week's repairs and payment. He wanted work locations, standards, a deadline, and an approved budget. I requested a list of defects and an itemized estimate, prioritized safety, and authorized no spending pending the one o'clock accounts review. I left before hearing any substantive reply. The secretary and builder spoke while I walked away, but I could not make out their words and cannot infer their subject. Both now appear to be walking toward the plaza. Several townsfolk are nearby, and the neighbour is farther west. These movements could simply be normal town business. I have tea with the neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage at three, which may be an opportunity to hear local news; I have not yet learned anything from them today. For now I should keep my appointments, hear residents' concerns during the market walk, and distinguish actual reports from my suspicions.
